subject.title: [Bug]: Google Chat: Space/Group messages silently ignored (DMs work correctly)

question: For Google Chat Spaces, should OpenClaw keep strict `botUser` mention matching, auto-detect or accept current Chat mention annotations more broadly, or recommend `requireMention: false` for HTTP-endpoint Spaces because Google already limits delivered Space events?
rationale: Source review shows the remaining drop path, but the permanent behavior affects Google Chat group security defaults and depends on live payload semantics that are not fully captured in the issue comments.

options.title: Fix Detection, Keep Secure Default
options.body: Keep `requireMention` as the default, improve Google Chat annotation matching or bot-user autodetection in the plugin, add diagnostics, and require live Space proof before closing.

options.title: Document RequireMention Off For Spaces
options.body: Treat Google's HTTP-endpoint delivery as sufficient activation for configured Spaces and document or migrate users toward `requireMention: false`, accepting the broader default behavior as intentional.

options.title: Consolidate Into Broader Space Work
options.body: Move the remaining behavior under the broader Google Chat Space/thread routing backlog if maintainers want one design to cover mention detection, threading, and all-message ingestion together.

recommendation.title: Fix Detection, Keep Secure Default
recommendation.body: Keep `requireMention` as the default, improve Google Chat annotation matching or bot-user autodetection in the plugin, add diagnostics, and require live Space proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the current Google Chat monitor/access/docs surface and is best placed to decide the group-activation default.
